words: ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power lets Him direct the morally responsible under His will, judgment, and wisdom; none can repel or prevent what He chooses.
rows.anchor: ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila argue that if God's speech were eternal, abrogating and abrogated passages would both be eternal, although abrogation requires succession and the abrogated passage to cease.
rows.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن القرآن مخلوق

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila infer createdness because the verse describes some Qur'anic passages as better than others, whereas what is differentiated this way is not eternal.
rows.anchor: أن الآية دلت على أن بعض القرآن خير من بعض

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila argue that God replaces abrogated passages through an act within His power, and any such act is originated.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أنه تعالى هو القادر على نسخ بعضها

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: Razi's side replies that abrogation belongs to words, expressions, and languages; it does not show that the actual meaning conveyed by them is originated.
rows.anchor: بأن كونه ناسخا ومنسوخا إنما هو من عوارض الألفاظ

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila answer that divine speech's first relation to a passage ceases and a later relation begins; since eternal things cannot cease, both relations are originated, and speech cannot be apart from them.
rows.anchor: ذلك المعنى الذي هو مدلول العبارات واللغات لا شك أن تعلقه الأول قد زال

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: Razi's side counters by analogy with God's power and knowledge: their earlier relation to a future world must cease when it exists, or else imply impossible power over an existing world or ignorance; the same answer applies to speech.
rows.anchor: أن قدرة الله كانت في الأزل متعلقة بإيجاد العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer seeks the actual attainment of Islam rather than a mere description: obtaining the thing itself is more desired than acquiring its label.
rows.anchor: أن الموصوف إذا حصلت الصفة له فلا فائدة في الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the prayer asked only for the label Muslim, their existing Islam made it pointless; God cannot falsely ascribe a quality they lack.
rows.anchor: أنه متى حصل الإسلام فيهما فقد استحقا التسمية بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating the request as mere naming would wrongly imply that anyone who called Abraham Muslim had thereby made him Muslim.
rows.anchor: لو كان المراد به التسمية لوجب أن كل من سمى إبراهيم مسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects interpreting God's making them Muslim as merely granting لطف, because the wording attaches the act of making to Islam itself.
rows.anchor: لفظ الجعل مضاف إلى الإسلام فصرفه عنه إلى غيره ترك للظاهر

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: On the Mu'tazila account, God had already provided and actualized those enabling graces, so asking for them again would seek an already achieved state.
rows.anchor: تلك الألطاف قد فعلها الله تعالى وأوجدها وأخرجها إلى الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A لطف either has no effect on preferring action, in which case it is no لطف, or affects preference; if so it must determine action or leave the outcome arbitrary and without a differentiating cause.
rows.anchor: تلك الألطاف إما أن يكون لها أثر في ترجيح جانب الفعل على الترك

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila appeal to rational proofs that God does not create human acts, since divine creation would undermine praise and blame; Razi answers with the prior objections from knowledge and motive.
rows.anchor: الدلائل العقلية دلت على امتناع وقوع فعل العبد بخلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi defers discussion of whether a supplicant should address God only as rabbana to his treatment of the conditions of prayer at 40:60.
rows.anchor: إن العبد لا يخاطب الله تعالى وقت الدعاء إلا بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min is partitive: Abraham and Ishmael ask for some of their descendants to be a Muslim community.
rows.anchor: واجعل من أولادنا و ( من ) للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for only some descendants because God had told them that some descendants would be wrongdoers (2:124).
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى أعلمهما أن في ذريتهما الظالم

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: Some interpreters take the descendants meant here to be the Arabs, since they descend from Abraham and Ishmael.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : أراد به العرب لأنهم من ذريتهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the requested Muslim community to be Muhammad's community, in light of the request for a messenger among them (2:129).
rows.anchor: قيل هم أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks why they prayed for a Muslim subset when 2:124 already implies that some descendants were not wrongdoers and some therefore were.
rows.anchor: قد بينا أن قوله : { لا ينال عهدي الظالمين } كما يدل على أن في ذريته من يكون ظالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that the earlier implication was not conclusive; an anxious, caring person is prone to worry and ask again.
rows.anchor: تلك الدلالة ما كانت قاطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks why Abraham and Ishmael singled out their descendants, as that might resemble miserliness in prayer.
rows.anchor: لم خص ذريتهما بالدعاء أليس أن هذا يجري مجرى البخل في الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their descendants especially merit compassion and care (66:6); righteous prophetic offspring help reform their followers, as upright early scholars and leaders guide later people.
rows.anchor: ولأن أولاد الأنبياء إذا صلحوا صلح بهم غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A questioner reasons that the prayer must have been answered because God did not explicitly reject it, but objects that Muhammad's Arab ancestors were not Muslim and no non-Arab descendants of Abraham and Ishmael existed.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الله تعالى لو رد هذا الدعاء لصرح بذلك الرد

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal replies that Abraham's descendants always included monotheists and prophets; before Islam Zayd ibn Amr, Quss ibn Sa'ida, reportedly Abd al-Muttalib, and Amir ibn al-Zarb worshipped one God, believed in resurrection and judgment, rejected carrion and idols.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : أنه لم يزل في ذريتهما من يعبد الله وحده

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr, in some transmissions, read arinā with a still rāʾ throughout the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو في بعض الروايات

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: Asim and Ibn Amir agree with the still-rāʾ reading at one place only, Fussilat 41:29.
rows.anchor: ووافقهما عاصم وابن عامر في حرف واحد ، في حم السجدة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: In some of his apparent transmissions, Abu Amr reads the rāʾ with a shortened kasra, without full articulation, throughout the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في بعض الروايات الظاهرة عنه باختلاس كسرة الراء

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use a full kasra; Razi prefers this majority reading because it preserves the word from excessive deletion and indicates the lost hamza.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالكسرة مشبعة ، وأصله أرئنا بالهمزة المكسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arinā originally had a hamza with kasra; its vowel moved to rāʾ and the hamza was deleted, while retaining rāʾ's vowel avoids undue loss of the word's form.
rows.anchor: نقلت كسرة الهمزة إلى الراء وحذفت الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The still-rāʾ form drops both the hamza and its vowel and analogizes to forms such as fakhidh and kibd.
rows.anchor: وأما التسكين فعلى حذف الهمزة وحركتها وعلى التشبيه بما سكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened kasra seeks ease while retaining an audible indication that the hamza was deleted.
rows.anchor: وأما الاختلاس فلطلب الخفة وبقاء الدلالة على حذف الهمزة

rows.speaker: من جوز الذنب على الأنبياء
rows.claim: Those allowing sin for prophets infer it here because repentance presupposes a prior sin; otherwise asking for repentance would ask for the impossible.
rows.anchor: احتج من جوز الذنب على الأنبياء بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila permit minor sins by prophets and take this as repentance from a minor sin.
rows.anchor: وأما المعتزلة فقالوا : إنا نجوز الصغيرة على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi objects that minor sins are already erased by the reward for their doer, so repentance to erase what is already erased is impossible.
rows.anchor: إن الصغائر قد صارت مكفرة بثواب فاعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer is that adopting repentance's posture strengthens resolve and restraint from sin, serving as an inducement to avoid it.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يأتي بصورة التوبة تشددا في الإنصراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that even diligent worshippers fall short through inattention or by leaving what is preferable, and seek repentance for that shortfall.
rows.anchor: فإنه لاينفك عن التقصير من بعض الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer takes the request as asking God to enable sinful descendants to repent; a compassionate parent can speak of a child's offense as his own.
rows.anchor: أن في ذريته من يكون ظالما عاصيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi supports reading the request as intercession for descendants with Abraham's prayer to avoid idols and his saying that whoever disobeys him is under God's mercy if he repents (14:35–36).
rows.anchor: في سورة إبراهيم أنه قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Abdallah says “show them their rites and accept repentance for them,” supporting the interpretation that the prayer concerns descendants.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن في قراءة عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following request for a messenger among the descendants supports taking “repent for us” as a prayer for the descendants' repentance.
rows.anchor: أنه قال عطفا على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi notes an interpretation of 7:11 in which creating Adam encompasses his descendants, making it possible to understand “show us our rites” as “show our descendants.”
rows.anchor: تأولوا قوله تعالى : { ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested messenger is from the same descendants as the Muslim community in the preceding prayer; that description fits Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: لا شبهة في أن قوله : { ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا } يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger among them completes their religion and law and calls them to remain steadfast in Islam.
rows.anchor: أن يكون فيهم رسول يكمل لهم الدين والشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having a messenger from their own descendants gives them greater honor and religious standing than a messenger from outside their lineage.
rows.anchor: لأن الرسول والمرسل إليه إذا كانا معا من ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger from among them makes it easier to know his truthfulness and trustworthiness because they know his origin and upbringing.
rows.anchor: إذا كان منهم فإنهم يعرفون مولده ومنشأه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger from their own people is more solicitous for their welfare and compassionate toward them than an outsider would be.
rows.anchor: إذا كان منهم كان أحرص الناس على خيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham sought to establish religion for his descendants both immediately and in the future, believing his aim would be most fully realized through them, with added joy and honor in that outcome.
rows.anchor: عمارة الدين في الحال وفي المستقبل

rows.speaker: إجماع المفسرين
rows.claim: Razi identifies Muhammad as the messenger and cites the commentators' consensus as proof.
rows.anchor: إجماع المفسرين وهو حجة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muhammad is reported to have said, “I am Abraham's prayer and Jesus' glad tidings”; Razi identifies Abraham's prayer with this verse and Jesus' glad tidings with 61:6.
rows.anchor: ما روي عنه عليه السلام أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham prayed in Mecca for descendants there and nearby, and God sent no messenger to its people and surroundings except Muhammad.
rows.anchor: إن إبراهيم عليه السلام إنما دعا بهذا الدعاء بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that knowledge cannot be under obligation through choice: necessary knowledge is involuntary, while theoretical knowledge either follows necessarily from sufficient premises or requires an earlier theoretical premise, producing regress; thus the request for repentance is literal and conflicting verses should be interpreted away.
rows.anchor: الداخل تحت التكليف هو العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for pairing Abraham with Muhammad in blessings is that Abraham prayed for Muhammad here, so God repaid the intimate friend by keeping his name on the community's tongues.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام دعا لمحمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Abraham's prayer for lasting good praise (26:84) was answered by joining his name to Muhammad's in the latter's community.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام سأل ذلك ربه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation calls Abraham father of the religious community (22:78) and Muhammad a father of mercy, citing Ibn Masud's reading, 9:128, and the Prophet's saying that he is like a father to believers.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم كان أب الملة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said he was like a father to the believers in compassion and mercy, another reason to pair him with Abraham in blessings.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( إنما أنا لكم مثل الوالد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation pairs Abraham, herald of the pilgrimage (22:27), with Muhammad, herald of faith (3:193), in remembrance.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام كان منادي الشريعة في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi gives two meanings for the signs recited: the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad, since that is what he recited, or proofs of the Creator and His attributes, which he reminded people of and called them to believe.
rows.anchor: أنها الفرقان الذي أنزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching the Book means directing people to recite it and teaching its meanings and realities.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنه يأمرهم بتلاوة الكتاب ويعلمهم معاني الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation preserves the Qur'an's wording through mass transmission, safeguards it against textual corruption, displays its miraculous wording and arrangement, and is itself worship, including in prayer.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن يكون لفظه ونظمه معجزا لمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest purpose is teaching the Book's proofs, rulings, meanings, wisdom, and secrets; therefore recitation is followed by teaching its deeper realities.
rows.anchor: الحكمة العظمى والمقصود الأشرف تعليم ما فيه من الدلائل والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is rightness in speech and action; one is wise only by combining both and placing each thing where it belongs.
rows.anchor: الإصابة في القول والعمل ، ولا يسمى حكيما إلا من اجتمع له الأمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may derive from ahkamtu, “I restrained”: wisdom restrains ignorance and error through sound speech and action.
rows.anchor: أصلها من أحكمت الشيء أي رددته

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal reports a philosophers' definition of wisdom as resembling God to the extent humanly possible.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : وعبر بعض الفلاسفة عن الحكمة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik, in an answer to Ibn Wahb, defines wisdom as knowledge of religion, understanding it, and following it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن وهب قلت لمالك

rows.speaker: الشافعي وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Qatada identify wisdom as the Prophet's Sunnah.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : الحكمة سنة رسول الله

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i's followers argue that because the verse separately mentions reciting and teaching the Book before wisdom, wisdom must be something outside the Book, namely the Sunnah; an objection asks why it could not mean rational proofs of monotheism, justice, and prophecy.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر تلاوة الكتاب أولا وتعليمه ثانيا

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: In response to the objection, al-Shafi'i's followers say that reason independently receives rational proofs, so wisdom here should mean knowledge not obtained except through revelation.
rows.anchor: لأن العقول مستقبلة بذلك فحمل هذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes wisdom as distinguishing truth from falsehood, a verbal noun meaning judgment; the messenger teaches God's revealed Book and the rulings and judgments God teaches him.
rows.anchor: الفصل بين الحق والباطل ، وهو مصدر بمعنى الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes “Book” as the unambiguous verses and “wisdom” as the ambiguous verses.
rows.anchor: أراد به الآيات المحكمة . ( والحكمة ) أراد بها الآيات المتشابهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the Book as its rulings and wisdom as teaching the rationale, benefits, and interests served by those laws.
rows.anchor: أي يعلمهم ما فيه من الأحكام . ( والحكمة ) أراد بها أنه يعلمهم حكمة

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: Some say all these descriptions are attributes of the Qur'an: it is signs, a Book, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : الكل صفات الكتاب كأنه تعالى وصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human perfection requires knowing truth for its own sake and knowing good in order to act on it; purification follows the mention of virtue by removing vice and deficiency.
rows.anchor: كمال حال الإنسان في أمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a messenger does not coercively control people's inner lives, purification means his other efforts—warnings, promises, exhortation, reminders, and practical engagement—strengthen their motives to believe and do good; Razi prefers this over the alternative.
rows.anchor: الأول : ما يفعله سوى التلاوة وتعليم الكتاب والحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is that the messenger testifies to their purity on Judgment Day, as a person certifying witnesses; Razi says the first interpretation better fits Abraham's prayer for his descendants' salvation.
rows.anchor: الثاني : يزكيهم ، يشهد لهم بأنهم أزكياء يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the messenger purifies them from polytheism; Razi infers that Ismail's descendants included ignorant polytheists whom the messenger would make wise after ignorance.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : يزكيهم : يطهرهم من شركهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets purification as obedience to God and sincerity.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : التزكية هي الطاعة لله والإخلاص عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes purification as removal of polytheism and other impurities, as in 7:157.
rows.anchor: ويزكيهم عن الشرك وسائر الأرجاس ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing praise calls God unconquerably powerful and all-knowing; His knowledge and power make His acts sound and free of absurdity, enabling answered prayer, messengers, and revelation.
rows.anchor: هو القادر الذي لا يغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aziz is an essential attribute when it means power over things and invulnerability to need or humiliation, since God has no needs and none can block His will.
rows.anchor: العزيز من صفات الذات إذا أريد اقتداره على الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “aziz” means invulnerability to another's control and “hakim” means wise acts, both are attributes of action; essence attributes are eternal and cannot have opposites, while action attributes are relative and depend on effects.
rows.anchor: إذا أريد بالعزة كمال العزة وهو الامتناع من استيلاء الغير عليه

rows.speaker: النظام
rows.claim: Al-Nazzam argues God cannot perform a vile act: essential wisdom excludes folly, and an impossible act cannot be within divine power.
rows.anchor: واحتج النظام على أنه تعالى غير قادر على القبيح

rows.speaker: النظام
rows.claim: Al-Nazzam reasons that if God's wisdom could be replaced by its opposite, Godhood without wisdom would result, which is impossible; wisdom and foolishness are intuitively incompatible, so God cannot do what is vile.
rows.anchor: لو لم يجب ذلك لجاز تبدله بنقيضه

rows.speaker: النظام
rows.claim: Al-Nazzam further argues that wisdom is intuitively incompatible with foolish action, and what entails an impossibility cannot be within divine power.
rows.anchor: الحكمة تنافي فعل السفه فذلك أيضا معلوم بالبديهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers al-Nazzam that on Razi's doctrine none of God's acts is folly, so the objection disappears.
rows.anchor: أما على مذهبنا فليس شيء من الأفعال سفها منه فزال السؤال
